script.title: Who blocked my request?

dialogue.speaker: taplu
dialogue.text: I called the API with a JSON body and got blocked by CORS. The server is literally running!

chat.display: called the API, CORS blocked me 😤 server is literally up

dialogue.speaker: jack
dialogue.text: Different origin, so before your POST I sent a preflight OPTIONS request asking if that's allowed.

chat.display: different origin → I sent a preflight OPTIONS first ✈️

dialogue.speaker: john
dialogue.text: I got an OPTIONS request I don't handle, so I answered without any Access-Control headers.

chat.display: got OPTIONS, replied with no CORS headers 🤷

dialogue.speaker: taplu
dialogue.text: So who actually blocked it? The server or the browser?

chat.display: so who blocked it?? server or browser?

pause.prompt: The preflight response had no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header. Who blocks the request?

dialogue.speaker: jack
dialogue.text: Me. The server never refused anything. I block the response because it didn't say your origin is allowed.

chat.display: me 🙋 the server never refused, I block when your origin isn't allowed

dialogue.speaker: john
dialogue.text: The fix is on my side: allow your origin. Two lines.

chat.display: fix is on my side, 2 lines ✅
chat.code:
from flask_cors import CORS
CORS(app, origins=[FRONTEND])

dialogue.speaker: taplu
dialogue.text: And no wildcard star in production. Got it.

script.takeaway: CORS is enforced by the browser; the server fixes it by sending Access-Control-Allow-Origin for the origins it allows.

questions.explanation: The server only sends headers; the browser decides whether the page may read the response.
